data.content_ref: inline:The target's 'last man standing' mechanism presupposes that the process of elimination converges on a finite survivor, but the target's OWN countercondition admits the fatal case: 'If the set of possible theories is infinite, meaning elimination never leaves a "best" candidate.' This condition is not hypothetical — it is actual. The space of possible theories is demonstrably infinite: any refuted theory can be salvaged by an ad hoc adjustment, and infinitely many unconceived, unrefuted theories always coexist with the currently preferred one. Consequently, there is never a 'last man standing'; there are always infinitely many theories standing. The entire evolutionary-elimination metaphor ('we have no other candidates left standing,' 'the others are dead') collapses, because the others are NOT dead — infinitely many survive untested. Once the pool is infinite, mere non-elimination cannot generate a preference; some additional criterion (degree of corroboration, severity of test) must rank the survivors, and that ranking criterion is precisely what the induction charge targets. The target thus fails its own stated countercondition and the metaphor it relies upon is mechanistically inapplicable.
